evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'it would only take within the next five to seven minutes of your time so that I can build an accurate code' — frames time but never delivers the 'quote you can depend on' framing or waits for a yes before proceeding into discovery.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves straight into logistics probing (address, floor, walk distance, box count) without asking 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer raised a concern mid-call ('I'm still concerned that perhaps what we're requesting may be outside the scope of your services') but rep acknowledged it without digging deeper; however, this was customer-initiated, not a probing follow-up, so the Two Layers Deep item doesn't cleanly apply here.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no structured concern-gathering in Section 2, so no reflection opportunity.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full — rep anchors to typical 1-bedroom move (2–3.5 hours), personalizes to the specific route (one hour away, skilled nursing to assisted living, basic furniture only), and gives a range: 'Estimated cost is $1,103' with minimum $720 at 2.5 hours.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Full — rep discloses trip fee ($210) upfront, explains hourly rate ($102/hour per mover), mentions 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments: 'once we go over that it will always be prorated into fifteen minute increments.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked — rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or solicits a gut reaction to the price before moving on.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full — rep delivers: 'if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.'
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Partial — rep mentions '$2,000 per move' and 'repair, replace and reimburse' but omits the no-deductible/no-fine-print framing. Says only 'we will provide up to 2000 dollars per move' and 'that is the repair, replace and reimburse for your items.'
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False — rep launches into the two promises section but never asks a closing version of 'Does that put those to rest?' After the promises, rep pivots directly to estimate without looping back.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked — after the customer declines to book ('I just don't think at this point in time that just moving the few pieces that we need to move so quickly is $720'), rep asks only 'would you like me to send you like an estimate with regards to this or not anymore?' — transactional, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you?' check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: False — rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never — rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' Instead, rep moves to sending an estimate and closes without a direct ask for the business.

top_strength: Rep gathered all four discovery basics cleanly (name, moving day, city-to-city route, approximate size) and built a personalized, anchored estimate ($720–$1,103) that directly addressed the customer's emergency move context and route distance.
coaching_note: Add Section 2's 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns?' before diving into logistics, then circle back to those concerns in Section 6 — this call skipped the entire concern-discovery layer, and ended without ever asking for the business or confirming any booking details.
